chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man vowed to God that if God cured his son from his illness, he would definitely send him to perform Hajj to the Sacred House of God. So God cured the son, but the father died. He (the Imam) said: 'The obligatory Hajj is incumbent upon the father, and some of his children will perform it on his behalf.' I said: 'It is obligatory upon the son who made the vow.' He said: 'It is obligatory upon the father from his third (of the estate), or his son may volunteer and perform Hajj on behalf of his father.' And whenever a person vows a Hajj while he still owes the Hajj of Islam, then if he performs it, it will suffice for both of them together. And if he performs it on behalf of another, it will also suffice for what he vowed. Narrated.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a vow to perform Hajj if the father dies before the son goes?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the distinction between the *Hajj al-Nadhr* (vowed Hajj) and *Hajj al-Islam* (obligatory Hajj), establishing that a single performance satisfies both if the vow was made while the obligatory duty was still pending. Scholarly commentary notes that the vow creates a debt on the father's estate, which the son may settle by volunteering, highlighting the flexibility in fulfilling devotional debts in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the principle that specific intentions (*niyyah*) in ritual acts can consolidate multiple religious obligations into a single act of worship.
